key_insight: PLD-driven high-entropy oxide thin films can combine extreme cation disorder with unexpectedly high epitaxial crystal quality, enabling "anomalous crystallinity" in metastable oxides.
engineering_relevance: This opens a materials-design path for tailoring defect chemistry, lattice tuning, and coherent heterostructures in oxide films relevant to advanced optoelectronic and solar-cell interfaces.
method: Uses pulsed laser deposition to grow far-from-equilibrium high-entropy oxide thin films.
Leverages epitaxial constraints and kinetic arrest to stabilize metastable compositions and structures.
Examines MgCoNiCuZnO plus fluorite, spinel, and perovskite examples to generalize the growth-chemistry relationships.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes observed chemical and structural behaviors, highlighting Co valence, Cu coordination, and full coherence in selected rock-salt films grown on MgO as key examples.
watch_item: Because these phases rely on kinetic stabilization and epitaxial matching, results may be sensitive to substrate choice, growth window, and cation chemistry.
paper_title: Epitaxial Oxide Thin Films with High Entropy and Anomalous Crystallinity
